title: A recording opens to watch, with the editing tucked away until you want it
goal: User 2026-09-25: 'When I open a video, it seems defaulted into a trim workflow. I'd prefer to be in playback mode where the edit tools are collapsed but can be expanded.' Cause: EditorState.swift:1430 selects the clip and calls setTool(.trim) when document.opensWithTrimInHand (ClipTrim.swift:161), the 'fast lane' from docs/design/video-surface.md 10.3 and an acceptance item of trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret. The user rejects it. Runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock (video.html) and Premiere/QuickTime expectations apply: would someone who opens a video in QuickTime or Premiere's source monitor expect this?
acceptance: Opening a recording selects nothing and picks no editing tool; it lands in playback: the picture fitted above the transport, play/pause with Space, the scrubber, time and volume

The editing chrome (timeline tracks, clip handles, video tool bar) is collapsed to the transport row, with one clear control to expand it (a chevron or an Edit button on the transport) and a shortcut; expanding animates open smoothly
Starting any edit expands it by itself: pressing B, I/O, T, Q/W, dragging on the scrubber with a modifier, right-click Split, or choosing Trim
Collapsed or expanded is remembered per user (the last choice sticks for the next recording), and a document you have already edited reopens expanded
opensWithTrimInHand and the 10.3 fast lane are removed from the code and from video-surface.md; the trim task's acceptance item that required it is struck with a note pointing here
A walk at Next defaults opens a recording, checks no tool is active and the dock is collapsed, plays, expands, and photographs both states

log.note: Adversarial review before building: (1) A QuickTime/Premiere source-monitor user expects picture + transport and nothing picked; today Trim is in hand and the clip picked, which is the complaint. (2) The mock (video.html .transport + #tlDock, dock.js/dock.css) keeps the transport and collapses the timeline to a 30pt rail under it: chevron, TIMELINE, the pick + time summary, 'click to expand'. That is what ships collapsed, so nothing new is invented. (3) Keys: J/K/L/space/arrows must keep working collapsed, so the timeline keeps the keyboard; edit keys (I/O, B, M, Q/W, ;/', ⌘K, ⌘T, zoom) open it. (4) Trim with nothing picked already finds the clip under the playhead, so dropping the fast lane costs one key, not a click. (5) Guides ring the tracks on their first card (cut-a-recording-down), so a guide's sample opens expanded. (6) No modifier-drag exists on the transport scrubber today, so that acceptance item has nothing to hook; noted rather than invented. (7) ~85 walks open a recording and then drive the timeline; the remembered choice must be forgettable per walk so they can say which state they start in. Plan: pure rules in PhotonzCore (which commands open it, how a document opens, the rail summary), a per-window video timeline state separate from the icon timing strip, remembered only on an explicit toggle.

Side by side with the mock (video.html .transport + #tlDock collapsed via dock.css .timeline[data-tl=closed] / dock.js .tlrail) against 1-opened-to-watch-sc.png: transport unchanged; rail matches the mock's row: chevron-up, TIMELINE uppercase faint, summary in mono ink (pick · time / length, just time / length with nothing picked, as the mock's data-tl-summary writes it), 'click to expand' faint at the right, ~30pt tall, hover lifts to glassThin. No layout, colour, control-type or copy-length differences found. Differences that are NOT this surface: soft first frame (a-recording-opens-on-a-sharp-first-frame) and the floating tool bar over the picture (a-picture-or-video-fits-above-the-tool-bar-not-u), both already open p1.

Walks: 92 walks that open a recording were run in batches. Guides (4) all pass. 27 needed the tracks showing or relied on the fast lane's pick; they now say setup.timelineOpen: true (new setup key: how a recording's timeline was last left by hand) and six pick their clip with selectRow. trim-is-a-tool now picks Trim up from the tucked state and proves Trim brings the tracks up. the-layers-row-says-how-many-pieces folds the tracks again after each cut, since a cut now opens them. Still failing exactly as in the 2026-09-25 sweep, not this task's: keys-copy-between-layers, punch-in-and-hold (now gets further, step 59 vs 17), captions-panel-keeps-its-margins (same step 25). a-recording-opens-sharp and a-guide-recording-opens-sharp are another runner's uncommitted walks using an unbuilt step; Scripts/test.sh is red on them alone (7 issues) and green (9819 tests) with them set aside, and they were put back untouched.

Left rough, not filed: dragging on the scrubber with a modifier has no gesture today, so nothing to hook (acceptance 3 otherwise met: B, I/O, M, Q/W, ;, ', ⌘K, ⌘T, S, zoom keys, right-click Split, Trim, and any document edit open it). Panel edits like Speed open the tracks too, by the any-edit rule; recorded in the audit's rough for the user to react to.

A recording now opens to watch: nothing picked, arrow in hand, timeline tucked to the transport plus the mock's one TIMELINE row; the row, × and ⌥⌘T open/close it and that choice is remembered; edit keys, Split, Trim and any document edit open it by themselves; edited documents and guide samples open expanded. Fast lane removed from code, video-surface.md §10.3 and the trim task's acceptance. Core TimelineOpening tested; Scripts/test.sh green (9819) with another runner's two unbuilt walks set aside; new walk a-recording-opens-to-watch-walk at Next defaults passes with 5 real window captures; 92 video walks run, 27 migrated to setup.timelineOpen, remaining failures identical to the last sweep.
